cleaned.normalization: NFC; U+200C/U+200D (ZWNJ/ZWJ) preserved as meaningful in Devanagari conjuncts, not stripped as zero-width noise
cleaned.language_filter_notes: langdetect has no 'bho' label, so it cannot itself catch Bhojpuri text misclassified as Hindi (they share vocabulary and script). The likely_bhojpuri count above is an ACTIVE reject filter (lexical marker comparison, see clean_lib.py marker_counts/BHOJPURI_MARKERS/HINDI_MARKERS), not a passive count: a document is dropped before reaching cleaned/ if Bhojpuri markers (e.g. बा/बाटे/एगो/गइल/भइल/कइल) outnumber Hindi markers (e.g. है/हैं/एक/गया) by >=2 hits. This is a coarse lexical heuristic, not a language model, and did not catch every case: scripts/remove_cross_language_duplicates.py found and removed 2 additional documents post-cleaning whose content was confirmed genuinely Bhojpuri (verb forms not in the fixed marker list) but had been sourced/labeled 'hin' by ai4bharat/sangraha while the same text was correctly labeled bho_Deva by HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-2 - an upstream labeling error, not introduced by this pipeline. That removal is the 'cross_language_content_duplicate_manual_removal: 2' row above; it is not part of clean_hindi.py's own drop_reasons counters, since it happened as a separate, later, targeted correction.

selection_rationale: Vocab utilization is already near-saturated by 8k (0.97625) versus 10k (0.9767, only 0.00045 higher) - the real jump in utilization is between 5k (0.9654) and 8k, not 8k and 10k. Fertility shows the same diminishing-returns shape: 5k->8k improves fertility 1.4961->1.3956 (6.7% relative), but 8k->10k only adds 1.3956->1.3583 (2.7% relative more) for a materially larger embedding cost. Byte-fallback rate (0.018301 / 0.019613 / 0.020213) is a narrow, roughly flat band across all three sizes and does not distinguish the candidates. At the embedding-parameter-budget level, assuming model_dim=512 (tied input/output embeddings, reproducing the TA-cited 24,000 x 512 = 12,288,000 = 49.15% of 25,000,000 that motivated the 5k-10k cap): 8,000 x 512 = 4,096,000 params = 16.38% of 25,000,000, versus 10,000 x 512 = 5,120,000 = 20.48%. Confirmed directly by the exact full-corpus count rather than inferred: 8,000 produces MORE total tokens than 10,000 (505,852,028 vs 491,883,387, measured separately for 10,000 before 8,000 was selected - smaller vocab means more tokens for the same text), pushing Hindi to 101.2% of the 500M-token target versus 10,000's 98.4%. 8,000 therefore captures nearly all of the achievable fertility/utilization gain over 5,000 at a meaningfully lower parameter cost than 10,000, with no offsetting benefit from going to 10,000.
